title: A Cross-Analyzing Approach to Sentiment and Bias Detection in Social Media: Insights from Geopolitical Conflicts
problem: During geopolitical conflicts, social-media discourse is contaminated by sentiment polarisation and systemic bias, making impartial situational awareness extremely difficult.
methodology: Built a cross-analysing ML/DL pipeline combining transformer-based sentiment classifiers with bias-detection heuristics over multilingual Twitter corpora, evaluated against human-annotated benchmarks.
impact: Surfaced quantifiable bias signals in conflict-era narratives and provided a reusable evaluation framework for information-warfare research.
description: Cross-analysing pipeline for sentiment and bias in geopolitical social-media discourse — surfacing measurable bias signals during conflict events.

title: Improving Monkeypox Outbreak Prediction Through Time-Series Forecasting with Machine Learning Models
problem: Public-health agencies needed earlier, more reliable forecasts of Monkeypox outbreak trajectories to plan response and allocation.
methodology: Trained and benchmarked LSTM, GRU and ensemble forecasting models on WHO outbreak time-series, with rolling cross-validation and uncertainty quantification.
impact: Produced forecast curves that improved short-horizon outbreak prediction over baseline statistical models, contributing to data-driven public-health preparedness.
description: LSTM/GRU/ensemble forecasting of Monkeypox case trajectories — improving short-horizon outbreak prediction for public-health response.
